Credit Agreements On July 31, 2025, the Company entered into two Credit Agreements (the first credit agreement being the “Commercial Credit Agreement” and the second credit agreement being the “Farm Credit Agreement,” collectively, the “Credit Agreements”). The Commercial Credit Agreement includes (i) a $ 500.0 million three-year unsecured term loan facility and (ii) a $ 600.0 million unsecured revolving credit facility. The Farm Credit Agreement includes a $ 500.0 million seven-year unsecured term loan facility. The proceeds of the term loan facilities under the Credit Agreements were fully drawn upon on September 2, 2025 to finance the Greif Acquisition. Loans under the Commercial Credit Agreement bear interest at the secured overnight financing rate (SOFR) or the base rate plus a margin, which, under the Commercial Credit Agreement, is determined based upon: (i) in the case of the revolving credit facility, our leverage ratio or debt rating, and (ii) in the case of the term loan facility, our debt rating. passages.text: FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS The following discussion and analysis of historical results of operations and financial condition should be read in conjunction with the audited financial statements and the notes thereto which appear elsewhere in this Form 10-K. This discussion includes forward-looking statements regarding our expectations with respect to our future performance, liquidity, ESG goals, and capital resources. Such statements, along with any other non-historical statements in the discussion, are forward-looking. See our discussion regarding forward-looking statements included under “Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors” of this Form 10-K. For our discussion and analysis of our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows for the year ended December 31, 2023, the earliest of the years presented in the accompanying audited financial statements included in Item 8 herein, please refer to our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on February 27, 2025. Such information is presented in Item 7 of such report under the subcaptions “Results of Operations —Year Ended December 31, 2024, Compared with Year Ended December 31, 2023” and “Liquidity and Capital Resources” and is incorporated by reference herein. Over view PCA is the third largest producer of containerboard products and a leading producer of uncoated freesheet paper in North America. We operate ten mills and 91 corrugated products manufacturing plants. Our containerboard mills produce linerboard and corrugating medium, which are papers primarily used in the production of corrugated products. Our corrugated products manufacturing plants produce a wide variety of corrugated packaging products, including conventional shipping containers used to protect and transport manufactured goods, multi-color boxes and displays with strong visual appeal that help to merchandise the packaged product in retail locations, and honeycomb protective packaging. In addition, we are a large producer of packaging for meat, fresh fruit and vegetables, processed food, beverages, and other industrial and consumer products. We also manufacture and sell UFS papers, including both commodity and specialty papers, which may have custom or specialized features such as colors, coatings, high brightness, and recycled content. We are headquartered in Lake Forest, Illinois and operate primarily in the United States. On September 2, 2025, we completed the acquisition of the containerboard business of Greif, Inc. for $1.8 billion in cash. The Greif containerboard business includes two containerboard mills with approximately 800,000 tons of production capacity and eight sheet feeder and corrugated plants located across the United States. The operating results of the Greif Acquisition are included in PCA’s results in the Packaging segment after the date of acquisition. Risks Related to our Operations, Business and Industry General Economic Conditions – A deterioration in general economic conditions may harm our business, results of operations, cash flows, and financial position. General global and domestic economic conditions directly affect the levels of demand and production of consumer goods, levels of employment, the availability and cost of credit, and ultimately, the demand for our products and the profitability of our business. The U.S. economy has experienced persistent inflation, and we have experienced, and continue to experience, cost inflation across our business. Inflation has resulted in, and may continue to result in, higher production and transportation costs, which we may not be able to recover through higher prices charged to our customers or otherwise. credit_strengths.text: PCA is the third largest North American containerboard producer and a leading uncoated freesheet maker, operating ten mills and ninety-one corrugated plants. This integrated scale supports pricing discipline and steady demand from food, beverage and industrial packaging customers, underpinning revenue growth across the last three fiscal years.

Operating cash flow covers capital spending comfortably, leaving free cash flow that funds dividends and buybacks. Cash generation has strengthened over the trend period, and the resulting free-cash-flow-to-debt ratio sits near the sector median, indicating internally funded deleveraging capacity.

key_risks.text: The Greif containerboard acquisition was funded with new term loans and senior notes, lifting reported debt sharply and raising gross leverage above the sector median. Integration execution and purchased capacity utilization must deliver the expected earnings contribution, or leverage could remain elevated relative to peers.

Persistent cost inflation across production and transportation may not be recoverable through customer price increases, and still-elevated interest rates could dampen consumer demand and raise borrowing costs. These disclosed pressures could compress margins and cash flow precisely as acquisition-related debt service steps up.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is strong and in line with the sector median, while the current ratio comfortably exceeds one. Cash on hand plus unused revolver capacity provide a solid liquidity buffer against the term-loan maturities falling due in the next few years.

The debt stack is laddered, with senior notes maturing across the late twenty-twenties and beyond, and no significant near-term maturities. However, the new term loans and farm credit facility carry floating-rate exposure, so coverage would narrow if short-term rates rise materially.

overall_credit_view.text: PCA's indicative financial risk profile is modest, with net leverage modestly above the sector median and cash-flow-to-debt comfortably inside the strongest tier. Headroom to the next leverage threshold is thin, so even a small EBITDA decline or incremental debt could shift the profile weaker.

Our forward view is that integration of the acquired containerboard assets and continued free cash flow generation should support gradual deleveraging, but shareholder distributions absorb most free cash flow, limiting the pace. We would monitor leverage and floating-rate exposure closely for any deterioration.

credit_strengths.text: PCA為北美第三大箱板紙生產商及領先的未塗布免費紙製造商，營運十間工廠及九十一間瓦楞紙廠。此整合規模支持定價紀律，並帶來食品、飲料及工業包裝客戶的穩定需求，支撐過去三個財政年度的收入增長。
營運現金流充裕覆蓋資本開支，留下自由現金流用於派息及回購。現金產生在趨勢期內增強，由此產生的自由現金流與債務比率接近行業中位數，顯示內部融資的去槓桿能力。

key_risks.text: Greif箱板紙收購以新定期貸款及優先票據融資，大幅推高報告債務，並使總槓桿率高於行業中位數。整合執行及購入產能利用率必須帶來預期的盈利貢獻，否則槓桿率可能相對於同業持續高企。
生產及運輸方面的持續成本通脹可能無法通過客戶價格上漲收回，而仍然高企的利率可能抑制消費者需求並提高借貸成本。這些已披露的壓力可能在收購相關債務償還增加的同時壓縮利潤率及現金流。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率強勁，與行業中位數一致，而流動比率舒適地超過一。手頭現金加上未使用的循環信貸額度提供了穩固的流動性緩衝，以應對未來幾年到期的定期貸款。
債務結構呈階梯式，優先票據在二十年代後期及以後到期，且無重大的近期到期債務。然而，新的定期貸款及農業信貸安排帶有浮動利率風險，因此若短期利率大幅上升，覆蓋率將會收窄。

overall_credit_view.text: PCA的指示性財務風險狀況為溫和，淨槓桿率略高於行業中位數，而現金流與債務比率舒適地處於最強梯隊之內。距離下一個槓桿率門檻的緩衝空間薄弱，因此即使EBITDA小幅下降或債務增加，也可能使狀況轉弱。
我們的前瞻觀點是，所收購箱板紙資產的整合及持續的自由現金流產生應支持逐步去槓桿，但股東分派吸收了大部分自由現金流，限制了速度。我們將密切監測槓桿率及浮動利率風險，以防任何惡化。
